critique.evidence: The screen usefully translates defense outcomes into attacker unit economics—attempt cost, success rate, successful-fraud cost, and ROI—and the before/after comparison supports the campaign-level defense narrative. However, its connection to intent integrity and the Mastercard brief is indirect: no protected payment intent, transaction flow, Mastercard-specific use case, fraud-loss avoidance, customer impact, or control-to-outcome attribution is shown. “Measured” ROI is asserted without visible formula, timeframe, sample basis, or provenance, and the remaining 25.60× attacker ROI weakens the claim that the business model has been defeated.
critique.fix: Show the causal chain from an intent-integrity control to blocked or challenged payment behavior and then to verified economics. Include formulas, timeframe, sample sizes, data provenance, attack spend and fraud-value assumptions, plus Mastercard-relevant outcomes such as fraud loss avoided, approval-rate impact, false declines, intervention cost, and defender ROI. Explain whether 25.60× is below an empirically justified attacker viability threshold.
